summary: Unexpected soft throttling after billing-tier upgrade; quota shows refreshed but 429s persist
description:
Issue summary: Customer reports persistent 429 (soft throttling) for a subset of requests immediately after upgrading their plan from dedicated -> enterprise. Console shows quota/top-up completed and tenant credits updated, but production traffic sees continued 429s for ~40 minutes. Impact: search indexing jobs and real-time chat flows intermittently fail for a subset (~12%) of workers, increasing latency and retries. Environment: prod us-east-1, mixed websocket and HTTP/2 clients.

Observed behavior:
- Customer upgraded plan at 2026-03-10T12:05:00Z via billing API.
- Console quota reflected new limits at 12:06:30Z.
- Error spike begins 12:08Z: rate-limit 429s with X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0 and X-RateLimit-Reset: ~12:08:30Z on some edge-nodes, while origin shows non-exhausted token counts.
- Spike subsided ~12:48Z after interventions (see resolution).

Why this is different from prior tickets: quota refresh is visible in control plane but refill/refill-window alignment across edge nodes appears delayed, causing a ‘soft’ 429 pattern (not global exhaustion). Customer-facing symptoms look like sustained throttling even though tenant credit balance is sufficient.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Have an active tenant on dedicated plan with sustained background workers (~300 concurrent requests).
2) Trigger a billing tier change (upgrade) using the billing API during a high-concurrency window, record the time.
3) Observe console shows quota/top-up success immediately.
4) Send steady traffic through a subset of edge nodes (simulate ~200 short-lived websocket sessions and 100 HTTP/2 multiplexed calls).
5) Watch for edge-level 429s while origin rate limiter reports available tokens.
logs_and_headers:
sample-client: curl -i -H 'Authorization: Bearer <key>' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
=> HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
   Retry-After: 8
   X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
   X-RateLimit-Sync-Id: edge-12/rsync-20260310-1206
comments: 2026-03-10 12:22 - Priya Kapoor (Support): Acknowledged, escalated to SRE. Asked customer for request timestamps, affected endpoints, and sample request IDs.

2026-03-10 12:30 - Customer (DocuSearch): Provided request ids: rq_az3, rq_b7f, rq_z12 and confirmed upgrade completed at 2026-03-10T12:05:00Z. Noted that only a subset of worker machines see the 429s.
2026-03-10 12:37 - Miguel Santos (SRE): Initial hypothesis: edge-level refill window lag after billing update. Collecting edge token sync metrics and control-plane publish timestamps.

2026-03-10 12:50 - Miguel Santos (SRE): Deployed temporary edge-sync patch (force-push refill_epoch) to edge nodes serving the tenant. Observed immediate reduction in 429s for affected nodes. Confirming stability.
2026-03-11 09:10 - Product (Ava Lin): Noted that this surfaced a race between billing commit and edge broadcast; adding a follow-up to ensure atomic broadcast semantics during top-up operations.
2026-03-11 11:05 - Priya Kapoor (Support): Notified customer of resolution and recommended best-practices for upgrades during high-concurrency windows. Customer accepted and closed the ticket.
investigation_notes: Edge nodes maintain a local token-window and rely on control-plane broadcasts to reset refill_epoch after billing changes. When the billing service wrote the new balance, the broadcast to edge sub-clusters sometimes lagged behind due to an intermittent NATS partition (~30s).
Edge logs showed consistent local refill_epoch values that did not match the origin's refill_epoch for ~20-40s, causing local remaining counters to report 0 despite global balance being updated.
Hypothesis confirmed by reproducer in staging: paused broadcast for 45s while applying top-up produced identical soft-429 pattern on subset of nodes.
Root cause: lack of idempotent, versioned broadcast with acknowledgement from edges. Control-plane assumed eventual consistency; under high-concurrency window this surface caused customer impact.
Risk: Transient but customer-visible throttling during billing operations or manual quota adjustments if the broadcast path experiences partitioning.
resolution_notes: Applied emergency hotfix: force-sync endpoint added to edge agent that accepts a refill_epoch and force-recomputes local token windows; invoked for the single tenant on affected edge subset at 2026-03-10T12:48Z.

Rolled a small control-plane change (PR github.com/redwood/inference/PR/4318) to publish top-up as a versioned message and require an ACK from edge sub-clusters; retried broadcasts until ACKs received. Deployed to canary 2026-03-11 02:00Z and to prod 2026-03-11 03:30Z.
Validated success: no recurrence after broadcast path reinforced; edges now report matching refill_epoch within <5s in normal conditions.
workarounds_provided: 1) For immediate relief, support can run edge force-sync for affected tenant (internal runbook: Confluence -> Rate Limiter -> Force Sync).
2) Recommend scheduling billing-tier changes during low-concurrency windows to minimize blast radius until broadcast ACKs roll out to all regions.
3) As a short-term client-side mitigation, throttle client concurrency (max parallel requests) during upgrade window or implement exponential backoff on 429s with jitter.
follow_up_actions: 1) Engineering to add end-to-end monitoring for broadcast ACK latency and create alert when >5s for >1% of edge nodes (assigned: SRE, ETA: 2026-03-18).
2) Product to update billing upgrade playbook to recommend background refill sync and show a progress indicator in Console (assigned: Ava Lin, ETA: 2026-03-25).
3) Dev to harden message publish retries and mark top-up events as strongly-consistent for enterprise tier (PR merged: github.com/redwood/inference/PR/4318).
4) Support to prepare KB article for customers explaining safe upgrade patterns and how to request immediate edge-sync (target publish: 2026-03-20).
